original_question: A support set in a Banach space X is a nonempty convex set C such that every point x of C is a support point, meaning there is a functional f on X with f(x) equal to the infimum of f over C and strictly less than the supremum of f over C. Which Banach spaces admit support sets, and do all non-separable Banach spaces have support sets?
target_in_paper: Section 12, Problem 18 (S. Rolewicz): "Which Banach spaces admit support sets? Do all non-separable Banach spaces have support sets?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target almost verbatim. It identifies the correct open problem in Section 12, includes both parts of Rolewicz's question, and gives the right support-set/support-point condition: every x in the convex set is exposed at the minimum of some dual functional, with that minimum strictly below the corresponding supremum on the set.
missing_details: Make explicit that the support set is a subset C of the Banach space X, and that "X admits a support set" means that there exists at least one nonempty convex set C subset X with the stated property.
Replace "a functional on X" by the standard Banach-space formulation "a continuous linear functional x^* in X^*".
State the quantifiers in full: for every x in C there exists x^* in X^* such that x^*(x) = inf_{y in C} x^*(y) < sup_{y in C} x^*(y).
If one wants the question to be fully stand-alone across scalar conventions, the ordered-valued dual-functional convention should be explicit; Section 12 leaves that implicit.

For paper-faithful context, Section 12 immediately notes Todorcevic's theorem that every Banach space of density omega_1 has a support set, and then isolates a different follow-up question (Problem 19) about density c; that contextual narrowing is not mentioned in the draft.
refined_question: Let X be a Banach space. Call a nonempty convex set C subset X a support set if for every x in C there exists x^* in X^* such that x^*(x) = inf_{y in C} x^*(y) < sup_{y in C} x^*(y). Which Banach spaces X admit a support set? In particular, must every non-separable Banach space admit a support set?
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 18 in Section 12, not at a broader neighboring issue. The introduction lists "Rolewicz problem on support sets" as one of the paper's main open problems, and Section 12 then states the problem in essentially the same two-part form as your draft. The nearby context in Section 12 defines support sets, records that every space with an uncountable biorthogonal system has a support set, states Todorcevic's theorem that every space of density omega_1 has a support set, and then formulates the non-equivalent remaining variant as Problem 19 for density c. Because your draft asks both for a characterization of spaces admitting support sets and whether all non-separable spaces have them, the closest paper-faithful stand-alone formulation is exactly Problem 18 with the dual-functional notation and existence quantifier made explicit.
